name: Talbot Carpet
desc: The near field behind a diffraction grating, sliced open along the optical axis — light that has only just left the slits keeps re-assembling itself into perfect copies of the grating at every Talbot distance, and the space between fills with the fractal lattice of fractional revivals, half-period ghosts and doubled-frequency images known as the Talbot carpet; because the self-imaging depth runs with wavelength, white light lays each colour's carpet at its own scale and the whole weave goes chromatic as the camera flies down the axis.

scale.doc: how much carpet is framed — grating periods across and Talbot depths down; harmonics are auto band-limited to whatever the buffer can resolve

speed.doc: rate of flight along the optical axis + grating morph rate

density.doc: source coherence — how sharp the fractional-Talbot detail stays (low = an extended source washing the fine weave out) plus grating duty cycle

tilt.doc: illumination tilt — shears the whole carpet along the propagation axis

hue.doc: colour cast; sets the laser wavelength in 'mono'

y.doc: where the framed slab sits along the optical axis

grating.doc: the grating being imaged: Ronchi bars, narrow slits, a pure phase grating, a seeded Dammann binary-phase array, or a plain sinusoid; 'auto' swaps it every section

seed.doc: seed — drift phases, Dammann transition set, plate grain
